#1823. Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Wirtz stars as Klopp’s side hit best form to top group

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:25

Germany thrashed the Netherlands 5-0 on Monday at the Olympiastadion in Berlin in the final round of the Nations League group stage.

In a convincing performance, the four-time world champions produced their best football since the arrival of Jurgen Klopp, who took charge of the national team after the disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.

With goals from Derry Scherhant, Nico Schlotterbeck, Brajan Gruda and Florian Wirtz, who scored twice, the Germans produced an impressive result against opponents who were also fighting for top spot in the group.

The victory took on even greater importance because of the situation before the match. Germany began the round in third place in Group A2, level on points with Greece and behind the Dutch, and risked missing out on the quarter-finals. With the win, they reached 11 points, overtook their rivals on goal difference and finished the first phase at the top, securing a place among the best eight in the competition.

One of the stars of the night was Derry Scherhant. Klopp’s selection on the left of the attack scored his first goal for the senior Germany team.

A native of Berlin, the 24-year-old winger, who plays for Freiburg, took the opportunity to make his mark in front of the crowd of his home city. His exuberant celebration after finding the top corner past Bart Verbruggen reflected the special significance of the moment in his international career.

The goal also rewarded the faith the manager has placed in the attacker. Scherhant was only making his fourth appearance for the national team and has earned his place amid the renewal carried out by Klopp since he took over.

The chance given to the Freiburg player is part of a strategy that seeks to widen the squad’s options, without restricting selections to the best-known names in German football. Against the Netherlands, the youngster delivered and showed that he can be an interesting option in attack.

Another standout was Wirtz, who again showed how his talent can make a difference in a Germany shirt. The attacking midfielder scored twice in the second half and was decisive in turning a lead built before the break into a rout. His ability to find space, accelerate attacks and arrive in positions to shoot gave another dimension to the German attack.

The performance reinforces one of the main positive certainties of the early days of Klopp’s reign: Wirtz is capable of taking on the team’s technical leadership.

As well as the brilliance of the number 17 and Scherhant’s first goal, the match also underlined the importance of the opportunities given to other young players. Gruda, who had already scored in the 3-1 win over Serbia, found the net again during this international break and has now scored two goals for the national team.

Left-back Philipp Treu was also among the starters, benefiting from the opening up of opportunities by the manager. These are names that help to give shape to a project still under construction and show that Klopp intends to increase competition in different positions.

It was a well-played and competitive first half, with good link-up play and quick transitions. At home, Germany had more possession and went for a proactive game, with a high line and patience to find space.

In the 41st minute, they found it: Scherhant received the ball on the right, got past Denzel Dumfries and curled a lovely shot across goal into the top corner past Verbruggen.

The Netherlands, for their part, took to the pitch practically already qualified. In their tactical approach in the first half, the Dutch opted for a more reactive game: either Xavi Hernandez’s team reached dangerous areas through counter-attacks, or they drew in the German press and built from the back, passing the ball patiently.

At the start of the second half, Germany needed only a few minutes to punish the visitors again. Fourteen minutes into the half, Wirtz began a move down the left, tried to play a one-two with Scherhant, but saw Dumfries step in front of him. The Liverpool midfielder then regained the ball, dribbled past the Dutch full-back and struck hard with his left foot from the edge of the area to make it 2-0.

From there it became a stroll. The Netherlands clearly felt the blow, and the hosts took advantage to turn the win into a rout. Schlotterbeck, with a header, Wirtz, with another stunning goal, and Gruda gave the match its final numbers.

#1820. "Magical" - German media rave over Liverpool star Florian Wirtz after 5-0 win vs the Netherlands

By Lewis Blain | 17 Nov 2026 07:18, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 07:24

Germany continued their impressive progress under former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp with a commanding 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday evening, with Florian Wirtz producing a standout performance.

The Reds midfielder scored twice in his 50th international appearance, including a spectacular left-footed effort, as Germany recorded their biggest victory over their neighbours since 1959.

Wirtz's display earned widespread praise in his homeland, with several publications awarding him the highest possible grade on the German school-style marking system, where 1 is the best, and 6 is the worst.

SPORT1 awarded Wirtz 1/6, describing his performance as "Ein magischer Abend des Hoffnungsträgers" - a 'magical' evening from the team's star of hope.

The publication acknowledged that he initially struggled to influence proceedings but praised his response after the interval, highlighting his spectacular first goal, subsequent brace-completing finish and ability to dictate Germany's attacking play. Sport Bild also hailed the Liverpool star's 'magic' on an impressive night.

FOCUS Online and Eurosport Germany also awarded Wirtz 1/6, with the latter describing him as the "überragende Mann" - the 'outstanding' player - after his two goals and impressive work out of possession.

FOCUS were particularly impressed by his response to an imperfect moment, joking that he had once dribbled the ball out of play unchallenged before showing his true quality with a "superb brace".

The Frankfurter Rundschau also handed him 1/6, describing him as the "Dreh- und Angelpunkt im Offensivspiel" - the 'focal point' of Germany's attacking play - while suggesting Klopp's system was allowing him to flourish.

Märkische Oderzeitung were slightly less generous, awarding Wirtz 1.5/6, but still praised his technical quality and two excellent finishes. They noted that he initially struggled to find decisive openings before becoming increasingly influential after the hour mark.

Sportschau did not provide a rating but similarly acknowledged that Wirtz was relatively subdued during the first half, before writing that he "Krönte seinen immer stärkeren Auftritt dann mit zwei Treffern" - capped his 'increasingly influential performance' with two goals.

The German media's enthusiasm inevitably raises the question of whether Wirtz can reproduce his international form more consistently at Anfield heading into a busy festive period.

There is little doubt that the 23-year-old has shown encouraging signs during his second season at Liverpool, registering two goals and five assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. However, these returns are still considerably below the extraordinary numbers he produced during his time at Bayer Leverkusen.

Wirtz registered 35 goals and 44 assists in 140 Bundesliga appearances for Leverkusen, becoming one of Europe's most exciting attacking midfielders. While adapting to English football and the Reds' demands takes time, he has yet to consistently reach those same creative and goalscoring heights for his club.

There have been encouraging developments, including scoring and assisting in their 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on November 8th, but the German's international performances are increasingly setting the benchmark for what supporters will expect.

His next opportunity to demonstrate that improvement comes in a huge Premier League encounter, with Liverpool welcoming Manchester United to Anfield on Sunday 22nd November.

After producing two goals against the Netherlands and earning a near-unanimous collection of top marks in Germany, Wirtz will return to Merseyside with considerable confidence. Klopp's influence on the national team has also provided an encouraging reminder of the football that Wirtz can produce when operating with freedom and confidence.

Liverpool will hope that his international brilliance can become a more regular feature at club level, particularly with one of their biggest fixtures of the season approaching.

As such, the 23-year-old, who is out of contract at Vitality Stadium in the summer of 2028, could be allowed to depart in the January transfer window for around £100million.

Manchester United transfer target Yasin Ayari appeared to pour cold water on any potential move to Old Trafford - before implying that he is keeping his options open.

JJ Gabriel has confirmed his decision to leave Manchester United in a statement, with Real Madrid expected to win the race to sign the highly-rated young winger.

The 16-year-old has played in United’s academy since 2020 and was expected to start appearing in the first team this season.

Until, that is, he made the shock decision to lodge a transfer request in September, amid reports he and his entourage were frustrated with his lack of first-team opportunities.

United worked hard to convince him to stay and offered him a new contract, but the player has not trained at the club for some time and is now expected to join Real Madrid. He will leave Old Trafford without having made a senior appearance.

After months of speculation as to where he might end up, Gabriel has now issued the clearest update yet on his situation, confirming his decision to leave United in a post to his Instagram page.

Speaking over clips of himself playing for the club, he said: “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.

“Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I’ll always treasure.

“To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”

Just in from the BBC, Arsenal in advanced talks with Piero Hincapie over a contract extension on improved terms.

Furthermore, discussions over new deal for Riccardo Calafiori are on the horizon.

#1817. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

While the Three Lions were beaten on that occasion, it would be a favourable draw given they have won two of the last three meetings against the Dutch - including the Euro 2024 semi-final.

The simulator hasn't been as kind to France as they've been paired with Spain, a team they have lost to three times in a row since victory in the 2021 final.

In addition, the simulator has thrown up two other eye-catching fixtures with Norway taking on Germany, and Portugal continuing the defence of their crown against Belgium over two legs.

#1816. Man United transfer news: Former defender backs move for Chelsea star Estevao

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 08:02

Mikael Silvestre sees Estevao as a player capable of strengthening Manchester United, but does not believe the Red Devils will pursue the forward at this time.

The former France defender, who played for the Old Trafford club between 1999 and 2008, praised the Brazilian’s performance and considered him an interesting option if he were available on the market. However, that prospect hinges on the young player’s willingness to fight for his place at Stamford Bridge.

Silvestre’s assessment comes at a time of significant change at Manchester United. The club invested more than £144m (€170m) in signings last summer and showed an intention to back Michael Carrick after the team finished last season in third place in the Premier League. The start of the new campaign, however, has fallen short of expectations.

The enthusiasm that had arisen among the fans was quickly replaced by dissatisfaction with the results. After the 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea, Manchester United reached nine consecutive matches without a win in all competitions. Neither the reaction against Roma, with a comeback in the Europa League, nor the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford was enough to prevent the departure of Carrick, who was sacked last Thursday (12 November).

Mauricio Pochettino has been chosen to take charge of the team. The Argentinian has officially left the United States national team and is expected to begin work at Manchester United this week, while the board is already focusing its attention on the January transfer window.

Among the possibilities to strengthen the squad, Estevao appears as a name that appeals to Silvestre. The 19-year-old Brazilian is still seeking greater playing time at Chelsea, but he had a standout performance precisely against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge.

In an interview with Betarades.gr, the former player highlighted the forward’s display and pointed to his determination as an obstacle to a possible transfer.

‘Estevao played for Chelsea against Manchester United, and I think he showed why he deserves more playing time. It looks like he is going to fight for his place, so I do not think Manchester United will make a move for him’ - Silvestre said.

The Frenchman’s interpretation is that the Brazilian intends to seize opportunities to establish himself at Chelsea rather than seek a move at this time. Even so, Silvestre left no doubt about his individual assessment of the player.

‘But he is definitely a good player. He plays for the Brazil national team, and I like his style of play. If he were available for transfer, he would be a good signing for Manchester United’ - he added.

Manchester United are set to return to the transfer market in January with the intention of improving the team’s performance in the second half of the season. One of their priorities is signing a left-back, a position for which the club unsuccessfully attempted to sign Lewis Hall from Newcastle in the summer.

The attacking department may also receive attention from the board. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, considered important players for the team, have had starts to the season below expectations, increasing the need to find alternatives in attack.

With Pochettino about to begin his tenure, planning for the next transfer window is gaining importance. Estevao, despite having Silvestre’s approval, would depend on a change of scenery at Chelsea to effectively enter Manchester United’s radar.

For now, the most likely scenario is that the Brazilian will remain in London trying to gain more playing time and consolidate his position at Chelsea.

#1815. Super Mario! Dons hand rebuild job to Swiss success story Frick

Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their new head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

Frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington said the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington said: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

Pfannenstiel said: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their new manager

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'

Before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

As a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

Frick said: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

#1814. Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners, relegation race, Golden Boot and more

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The 2026-27 Premier League season is just days away from resumption following the final international break of the year, and with it the return of some familiar faces.

Mauricio Pochettino is back in English football after a spell in international management, he has succeeded Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach. Meanwhile, Thomas Frank has replaced Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace.

After 10 games of the campaign, both Man United and Palace are in the relegation zone. So will these appointment help to drag them out of the bottom three?

At the other end of the table, Arsenal have made a solid start to the defence of their Premier League crown, and appear to have a surprise challenger as confusion has set in around Manchester City.

Plenty of questions to be answered over the next six months, and the Standard Sport football reporters, Matt Verri, Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau, have had a go at predicting what is in store for the remainder of the season.

MV: Arsenal continue to look ruthlessly efficient and should be confident of defending their title. The defensive unit is absurdly good, the midfield depth is ridiculous, and it means the forwards only need to deliver a moment or two per match.

Even whey they are not at their best, Arsenal are just so difficult to beat. That is the case over 90 minutes and it should be the case over 38 matches again.

DS: No reason to change what I predicted at the beginning of the season, which was for Arsenal to win the Premier League title. If anything, the opening 10 rounds of games have made me more convinced the Gunners won’t be caught and will defend last season’s crown.

Arsenal fans may continue to worry about a lack of goals from their forwards, but their defence is on track to perform even better than last season’s, and that gives other challengers a daunting task to catch them. Arsenal could genuinely win the title by as many as 15 points.

ST: Arsenal were favourites to retain the Premier League title before the season started and that has not changed 10 games in.

Chelsea have the firepower in attack to secure fourth and Unai Emery can work his magic to get Aston Villa into fifth.

DS: My top five, in order, back in August was Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea, then Liverpool. That needs some revising.

Man City are difficult to predict because of the unknowns involved in their impending punishment for financial rule breaches, but they may just about hold on to second (pre-punishment). In third, there are signs Liverpool could come good, particularly if Alexander Isak can stay fit.

Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea are all interchangeable. But I think it will end up being City second, Liverpool third and Chelsea fourth.

MV: Assuming a resolution is reached this season, it is hard to see how Manchester City can avoid a sanction that leads to relegation. DS: Along with many others at the time, I predicted the three promoted teams to go straight back down. Even though Hull made a good start, Ipswich have been decent and Coventry seem to have turned a corner, I still expect those three to be weaker than Sunderland, Fulham, Crystal Palace and other strugglers as the many months progress. Coventry, Hull and Ipswich still.

I think Fulham, Nottingham Forest and Coventry are all capable of getting dragged into the relegation zone.

Sunderland, Forest and Coventry will be the three to go down.

MV: Thierno Barry gets enough chances in front of goal to challenge, while Alexander Isak is starting to show why Liverpool were so determined to sign him. However, it is hard not to be boring. Even with the circus surrounding City, Erling Haaland will almost certainly secure another Golden Boot.

Joao Pedro would be the one I might have backed to challenge him, but injury has stalled his challenge.

DS: Why would it be anyone other than Erling Haaland? It says a lot that even after the Norwegian was criticised in some circles for failing to score in City’s last two league games, the defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest, he is still sitting pretty on top of the leaderboard with nine goals in 10 league games.

The Golden Boot simply won’t be won by anyone else.

ST: It’s the boring answer but in a league lacking natural goalscsorers, Erling Haaland is the obvious pick. The Norwegian has been off the boil in recent weeks, but he always finds his way back into form.

No one knows where the back of the net is quite like Haaland. It’s that simple.

The Argentine flew straight from the United States in the early hours of Wednesday morning and the Gulfstream G700 he was believed to be on was spotted landing at Manchester airport shortly before midday.

It was announced last week that the former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss was making a return to the Premier League, succeeding Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

However, the 54-year-old’s start to his fourth spell in English football was delayed as he finished up commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT), overseeing an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals in his last game in charge.

Now after touching down in the UK, Pochettino can now take the next step in his career.

“I am ready [to return],” he told the Telegraph. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

Pochettino is expected to head to Carrington immediately as he settles into his new role as Man United head coach, with the focus already shifting to his first game in charge against Liverpool on Sunday.

#1810. ‘There are different ways of winning’, says Mead after Man City edge out Hacken

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Beth Mead said "there are different ways to win football matches" after Manchester City battled their way to a 2-0 victory over Hacken.

Man City made it back-to-back wins in the Women's Champions League on Wednesday, thanks to second-half goals from Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw.

Andree Jeglertz turned to star attackers Hemp and Shaw at half-time at Nordic Wellness Arena, with City having failed to make the breakthrough in the first period, despite creating chances worth a combined 1.08 expected goals.

Hemp's introduction paid dividends when she opened the scoring in the 55th minute by bundling home while challenging for the ball. She then teed up Shaw to put the result beyond doubt late on, before Mary Fowler missed a stoppage-time penalty.

City finished with 3.43 xG, and while they were not at their clinical best, Mead, who was taken off for Shaw, was more than happy with the performance.

"It was a tough game – we had to work hard for the three points," she told UEFA.

"I'm really proud. It's been a busy schedule. Every player has been bringing different energy to the pitch – a different kind of pitch to play on, obviously. Everybody in the team turned up today and we did what we needed to do.

"There are different ways of winning football matches. Coming away from home in the Champions League is difficult but we found a way to win today."

— Manchester City Women (@ManCityWomen) November 18, 2026

Jeglertz, meanwhile, said City got exactly the game they were expecting.

He told UEFA: "A good game. We knew it would be a tough game to score against a very organised defending team. They have a great goalkeeper and we struggled in first half. In the second half, they got a little bit tired, we got a little more space and we managed to get the goals.

"We try to get the best out of each player and put them in positions where they can really show what qualities they have.

"We have a great team together, we rotate players, and they all have a great impact on what we're doing. I think that will be very important in the future."

City have lost just one of their 11 group stage/league phase games in the Champions League (W6 D3), losing 0-3 to Barcelona in December 2024.

#1808. Pedro Porro to Barcelona: Could Spain international move to Camp Nou in January?

By Matt Law | 17 Nov 2026 08:23, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 08:25

Barcelona will reportedly not make a move for Tottenham Hotspur defender Pedro Porro during the January transfer window, but a switch to Camp Nou next summer is a possibility.

Porro, 27, has had his issues at Tottenham, but the right-back was outstanding for Spain at the 2026 World Cup and is an important player for the national side.

There has recently been speculation surrounding Porro's future, with Barcelona planning to be active during the January market due to their defensive issues.

Barcelona had allegedly been open to the idea of signing Porro in the winter market, providing that a suitable deal could be agreed with Tottenham.

According to journalist Matteo Moretto, the La Liga champions will not be moving for Porro when the January window opens for business.

However, a future switch to Camp Nou has not been ruled out, with Barcelona potentially reigniting their interest during next summer's transfer window.

Porro said at the end of last month that he wants to return to La Liga before the end of his career.

"Obviously, I’d love to return to Spain someday. It’s my country, and I like the league," he told El Larguero.

"Right now, it would be very unfair to talk about anything other than my club because I’m under contract, but obviously, I’d love to go back to Spain; it’s a big dream of mine."

Porro also recently said that he was 'flattered' to be of interest to Barcelona.

"Yes, of course it's flattering," he said in an interview with SPORT.

"When one of the best clubs in the world is interested in you, or at least that's what they say, it's always a good thing, because it probably means I'm doing my job well. I have to keep going in the same direction."

Porro has previously played in La Liga for Girona and Real Valladolid, but he has not operated in Spain since 2020.

The right-back joined Tottenham from Sporting Lisbon in January 2023, and he has represented his North London club on 159 occasions, scoring 13 goals and registering 26 assists in the process.

#1806. Manchester United urged to target ‘established Premier League leader’ as Bruno Fernandes replacement

Former Manchester United winger Ashley Young has revealed he would replace Bruno Fernandes with Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Fernandes's contract expires at the end of this season, though United can extend their captain’s deal by an additional year and also prevent him from speaking to foreign clubs in January about a potential free transfer.

United want Fernandes to stay, but the 32-year-old has already turned down two new contract proposals as he weighs up his options following more managerial turnover at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his first training session on Wednesday after leaving the US men’s national team to replace Michael Carrick as United head coach.

Fernandes enjoyed a superb campaign last term, breaking the single-season Premier League assist record to help United qualify for the Champions League.

This season, however, he has struggled to replicate the same form, and he drew criticism after calling into question Carrick’s tactics following United’s 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como in October.

While Young admits there is no doubt about Fernandes’ contribution to United, with the Portuguese midfielder producing 75 goals and 74 assists in 239 Premier League appearances, he insists that in order for the Red Devils to move on, they should look to replace the former Sporting man with England international Gibbs-White.

“Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young tells Standard Sport.

“There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White.

“I think he's got 18 months left on his contract. He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

#1802. Chelsea and Manchester United lead tributes as Juan Mata announces football retirement

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea and Manchester United led the tributes to Juan Mata after he announced his retirement from professional football.

The former Spain international, who lifted the 2010 World Cup and 2012 European Championship, has hung up his boots at the age of 38 after leaving Australian giants Melbourne Victory in September.

Mata started his career at Real Madrid’s academy before moving to Valencia in 2007, where he won the 2008 Copa del Rey alongside fellow future World Cup winners David Silva and David Villa.

He moved to Chelsea in 2011 and helped the Blues win the Champions League and FA Cup in his first season at the club. The diminutive midfielder was crowned Chelsea’s Player of the Year in both of his two full seasons in west London before leaving for Manchester United in January 2014.

Mata helped United win the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup before his departure in 2022. He then spent the latter years of his career with Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

Mata announced his retirement with a 50-second video posted on his social media channels.

In the video, Mata sits in a changing room, staring at a pair of football boots. He then turns around and hangs them up on a peg, with the caption: “Sometimes to love is to let go. Thanks, football.”

A full statement was also posted on Mata’s official website, in which he admitted “Football will never leave my life” and that he would continue to use football “as a vehicle for development.”

Mata is best known for co-founding Common Goal, a global movement in which players, coaches, and clubs pledge at least 1% of their salaries to fund grassroots football charities.

“I was able to keep going for so many years because of the sheer joy of playing. Waking up every morning looking forward to training and playing, whether at magnificent grounds such as Old Trafford, Stamford Bridge or Mestalla.

“Or back when I was starting out at Juventud Estadio, where the pitch turned into a mud bath every winter. I believe that kind of passion is fundamental to everything in life.

“Over time, I realised football was about more than just kicking a ball. As I grew older, travelled and lived in different countries, I came to understand the power of sport in general, and football in particular, to change people’s lives.

“Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.”

Manchester United paid tribute to Mata, who scored 51 goals in 285 games for the Red Devils, with a post on social media.

“Great player, better person. Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan,” they wrote on social media.

Chelsea also posted a tribute to Mata on their social media pages.

“What a player,” Chelsea wrote in response to his retirement announcement.

#1801. England’s Ivan Toney fails in bid to move assault trial over Euro 2028 clash

Get our award-winning daily news email featuring exclusive stories, opinion and expert analysis

Ivan Toney’s bid to move the date of his assault trial to avoid clashing with Euro 2028 games has been refused by a judge.

The England footballer, 30, hopes to be selected to play for the national side in the next European Championship after featuring in this summer’s World Cup .

Toney is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6, 2025.

He denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a three- to four-day trial was fixed for June 12, 2028, which is three days into the Uefa Euro 2028 tournament.

At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, which Toney did not attend, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: “It came to our attention that… there may be potentially a football match called the European championships in 2028 between June 9 and July 9.”

Mr Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: “We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.

“My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup.”

Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a “speculative” application.

He refused the request, saying: “It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed.”

The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.

An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Mr Da Silva.

It was heard the two men “squared up to each other”, before Toney allegedly “lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches”.

The Metropolitan Police investigated and the footballer was charged in late July.

Toney, of Northampton, has made 10 international appearances and scored one goal.

He missed out on the latest squad for the country’s Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

#1800. Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Jurgen Klopp sends clear message that spells trouble for Nations League rivals

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 09:46

Jurgen Klopp is in dreamland after witnessing a “truly extraordinary” performance from his Germany side in a statement 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.

The four-time world champions began the night sitting third in League A Group 2 and knew that they had to claim maximum points against the Oranje at the summit to secure top spot and qualify for the quarter-finals.

With so much at stake heading into the sixth and final matchday, Die Mannschaft rose to the occasion in prolific fashion, claiming their biggest win against their Dutch neighbours since 1959 when they won 7-0.

Derry Scherhant opened the scoring just before half time with a sensational maiden international goal, setting the tone for a dominant second-half display.

Overwhelmed by Germany’s relentless high press, the Netherlands had no answer as two goals from Florian Wirtz, and strikes from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda, sealed a statement triumph for Klopp’s side.

“What we’ve just witnessed was truly extraordinary,” the former Liverpool manager told reporters post-match. “The game was extraordinary, and incredibly difficult.”

“Against a really good opponent, you have to find a way to win. We had to adapt and make a few adjustments, some fairly significant ones, but we made them. We took away a lot of their strengths, and then we scored some incredible goals. That was unbelievable.

“It was a fantastic football match and a wonderful experience. I wouldn’t have ever dreamed of having the chance to do this in Berlin in front of a sold-out crowd. In the final international game of the year, it’s amazing.”

In addition to progressing to the quarter-finals, the result served as compelling evidence of Germany's renaissance and progress under Klopp, with his arrival fostering renewed optimism around his youthful squad.

Germany failed to win their opening two Nations League matches, but they ended their group campaign with 11 points (W3 D2 L1) and have conceded a competition-low three goals in six games.

"The moment I arrived here, I fell in love with this team at first sight,” said Klopp. “I'm at the beginning of this journey.

“I simply feel that we have a fantastic football team and a very good footballing idea that can work extremely well. If we can get these highly-talented players firing, then we're going to be a very difficult team to play against.

“We scored some incredible goals and, with increasing confidence, put in a great performance in front of a fantastic crowd. It’s been a lot of fun to work with this team, and we feel like we have a very special group of players here.

“But this is still only just the beginning – after six games, we can’t say that we’ve arrived where we want to be yet, as there are still lots of things we can improve on.”

"Everyone who was here today is going home with a smile, and won't be questioning the German national team for the next three or four months. That's a good thing," Klopp added when referring to the negativity that lingered previously around the national team.

Looking ahead to the quarter-final draw on Friday, Klopp added: "The lads can head home now with a smile on their faces as the group winners. We’ll watch the draw later this week and wait and see what sort of crunch match we’ll get, as there are only strong teams left.”

Germany, who have risen to 11th in the FIFA World Rankings, will play their two-legged quarter-final tie in March 2027, with a first-placed finish in League A rewarded with a second leg on home soil.

#1799. Moreira discusses first Belgium goal, ‘special’ Milan group and learning in Italy: “I’ll always remember”

Last night, Diego Moreira scored his first goal for Belgium and AC Milan will be very happy to see their investment continuing to shine.

It’s fair to say that Moreira has been a revelation for Milan. His arrival came out of nowhere, with a deal first reported by FootballKush and then it was picked up by the biggest sources in football. His first appearance was a struggle against Juventus, but the rest, as they say, is history.

Goals have come regularly, with huge appearances that have defined the Rossoneri’s season already. For example, the goal against Inter, with two assists to accompany it. He’s perhaps been the signing of the season in Italy and there’d maybe be a conversation about Europe, too.

After scoring against Italy, Moreira spoke to Sky, looking at the team’s performance, playing with Kevin De Bruyne and the feeling of grabbing his first goal for his country, as MilanNews relays.

“I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”

Mancini said that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team…

“We have some very strong players up front, like Doku, De Bruyne, but I think that in the end it’s a sport where everyone is needed and we all played a great game.”

What does it mean to play with a player like De Bruyne?

“De Bruyne is special; it’s a pleasure to have him with us because he sees things that others don’t see, he has a lot of experience and we’re happy to have him in our team.”

What do you take from this experience with the national team at AC Milan?

“I learned a lot in Italy because it’s a league with a lot of experienced players. Playing for the national team and for AC Milan are two very positive things, and I’m very happy.”

How do you recover in Europe after a difficult start?

“It’s difficult but we’re working towards this. We have to be prepared and we have players who will help us with this.”

Then, in the mixed zone, he was also intercepted by MilanNews, where he also answered a few questions about the Rossoneri.

Diego, you scored in your first Milan derby, just like Kaká, Shevchenko, and Ronaldinho before you. How have you settled in at AC Milan?

“I’m very happy. At AC Milan, I’m surrounded by a special group, with many great players. Having them around me helps me a lot, especially in terms of experience. It’s true, the match against Inter was special. I’ll continue to work hard and give my best.”

Good in Serie A, bad in the Europa League: why this two-faced Milan?

“I’m on the national team right now, and you’re asking me about Milan?”

Belgium practically overwhelmed Italy, your current footballing nation. It ended 4-1, but the scoreline could have been eight or nine goals…

“It’s something special, and we’re very happy. It was an important match, so winning and scoring was really nice.”

#1798. Arsenal contract negotiations no longer a major source of stress as transformation complete

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The international break has played out something like an Oprah Winfrey show for the Arsenal squad.

Oprah, back in 2004, marched around her studio, declaring all those in the audience had won a car. Just the 276 Pontiac G6s dished out, for those wondering.

Andrea Berta has seemingly been following that example at Arsenal. “You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!”

It started with the news that Declan Rice had reached an agreement over a new long-term deal, one that will see him join Bukayo Saka on around £350,000-a-week.

Jurrien Timber, too, is set to commit his future to the club. Like Rice, he had entered the final two years of his current deal but the intention was always for Arsenal to tie him down beyond that.

There was more. David Raya has agreed fresh terms as well and will sign a new contract, a year on from receiving a pay rise. This deal will keep him at Arsenal through to 2030.

Piero Hincapie wanted in and is understood to have joined the extension club. The defender only signed for the Gunners permanently in the summer and that deal did not expire until 2031.

However, Hincapie has been rewarded with improved terms for his contribution to the title-winning season and a 12-month extension on the previous deal.

A busy period, then, for those involved in the building and managing of this squad. An extremely indicative one, too, both of how far Arsenal have come and where they want to get to.

It was not that long ago that contract negotiations for key players were a major source of stress for the club.

Under Arsene Wenger, Alexis Sanchez made it clear he had no desire to sign a new deal. Arsenal decided not to sell and he went into the last year of his contract, before joining Manchester United in a swap deal with Henrikh Mkhitaryan.

Terrified of losing Mesut Ozil for free and having been dragged into the final six months of his deal in 2018, Arsenal threw the kitchen sink at him and gave him a £350,000-a-week deal.

For years, Arsenal fans knew exactly when the contracts of the most important players would run out, almost fearing the two years leading up to that.

Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners and more

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal in Vinicius talks; Man Utd deal confirmed

Arsenal get new Havertz penalty review as Premier League panel confirm error

Not so now. Rice has entered the final 18 months of his existing deal but there was no real sense of jeopardy. The assumption was always that an extension would be agreed and that has proved correct.

This is now a club that players want to sign but just as crucially want to stay at. Rice’s new deal will commit his prime years to the club, as will be the case with Raya.

You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!

Had Rice wished to explore his options elsewhere, he would have had his pick of the elite clubs across Europe, as would William Saliba before he signed a new deal last year.

Arsenal might not be able to sign the most high-profile players from clubs like Real Madrid, as the summer pursuit of Vinicius Junior showed, but they can now protect their own assets regardless of who wants them.

There are still decisions to be made over other situations. Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz are both out of contract in 2028 as it stands. So too is Ben White and it is understood that as with Odegaard, no contract talks have yet taken place with the club.

However, the dynamic is very different to the one Arsenal have had to put up with in the past. These are not desperate negotiations. If these are players are leave in the transfer windows ahead, it feels like that would be a club-led decision.

These contract extensions also point to the power Mikel Arteta has and the priorities of the club. This is not about building a squad for five or six years down the line. Everything is centred towards giving Arteta the tools to win immediately.

That was apparent in the summer signings of Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes, both now 29, and in the handing out of huge contracts to take players well into their 30s.

Arteta has signed a contract of his own through to 2030 and it is all about maximising every opportunity for major trophies between now and then.

His priority is this season and the three beyond it. What happens after that, in terms of the age profile of the squad or the contract situations in the squad, might not be Arteta’s problem.

By then he might be driving off into the sunset. Probably not in a Pontiac G6.

#1797. Aston Villa transfer news: Newcastle United 'making strong moves' for Belgium international

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 09:54

Aston Villa and Newcastle United have reportedly identified Lille defender Nathan Ngoy as a potential transfer target.

Unai Emery's and Matthias Jaissle's sides went into the November international break sitting in 10th and 12th place respectively in the Premier League table.

Not only will both managers be disappointed with those positions, there will be concern that with their respective defensive records.

Villa have conceded 17 goals from their 10 top-flight fixtures in 2026-27, while the Magpies have shipped one goal fewer.

Therefore, strengthening in that area of the pitch has become a priority for the two managers ahead of 2027.

According to MilanNews24, Villa and Newcastle are 'making strong moves' to sign Belgium international Ngoy.

In sharp contrast to the two Premier League clubs, Lille have only conceded seven goals in 10 Ligue 1 fixtures, with Ngoy featuring in nine of those matches.

The 23-year-old has quickly become an established figure for his country, starting all six of their recent UEFA Nations League matches and scoring in the 4-1 win over Italy on Sunday.

While he possesses a contract at Lille until 2029, it remains to be seen whether Lille would be able to reject any substantial offers for his signature.

AC Milan have also been credited as admirers of the former Standard Liege player, who can deputise at right-back when required.

Although Villa signed Taylor Harwood-Bellis during the summer, he has not been viewed as a like-for-like replacement for Ezri Konsa.

Instead, Emery has been relying on three centre-backs in Victor Lindelof, Pau Torres and Tyrone Mings who are all aged between 29 and 33, essentially ensuring that alternatives will eventually need to be found.

Newcastle are in a similar position, with Fabian Schar and Dan Burn both aged 34 and right-back Tino Livramento having suffered regular injuries.

In both cases, Ngoy could become a first-team player should he move to Villa Park or St James' Park next year.

#1796. Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United: Will Things Finally Change at Old Trafford?

When Mauricio Pochettino walks into Anfield for his first match as Manchester United manager, he will immediately be confronted by the scale of the challenge ahead. There are easier ways to begin a reign than an away trip to Liverpool, especially for a club that has spent much of the past decade searching for stability and finding very little of it.

The symbolism is obvious. Liverpool have spent recent years building coherent teams, developing clear identities and competing regularly for major trophies, even if they did hit a few bumps on the road themselves. Manchester United have spent the same period cycling through managers, rebuilding projects and tactical resets. Pochettino’s appointment represents another attempt to break that pattern, but it would be a mistake to believe the Argentine’s task begins and ends with improving results.

His predecessors discovered that managing the team is only part of the job. The harder challenge is changing the culture and structure of a club that has repeatedly undermined its own attempts at renewal.

Pochettino was right to push back against the idea that Manchester United’s problems can be reduced to distance covered or sprint numbers.

The statistics are alarming. United have been outrun in most of their league matches and rank near the bottom of the division in several physical metrics. Yet simply demanding greater effort is unlikely to transform a struggling team overnight.

What United have lacked for years is collective purpose. Too often the team has looked like a group of talented individuals operating with different interpretations of the same game plan. When Pochettino talks about players running together and understanding their roles, he is really describing something more fundamental than fitness. He is talking about creating a collective identity.

That was one of the defining strengths of his best Tottenham side. They were physically outstanding, but their success came from organisation and belief as much as athleticism. Every player understood what was expected of him, and the team functioned as a coherent unit.

Manchester United have not consistently looked like that under any manager for a very long time.

It’s official. Mauricio is a Red 🔴📸 https://t.co/9uq47U3S3Z

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 18, 2026

The obvious counterargument is that other highly regarded coaches have arrived at Old Trafford with similarly ambitious ideas.

Erik ten Hag was respected throughout Europe. Ruben Amorim arrived with a reputation as one of the continent’s brightest tactical minds. Others before them possessed impressive credentials too.

What makes Pochettino different is the nature of his previous achievements.

Unlike some elite managers, he has rarely inherited finished products. His reputation was built on developing teams, improving players and creating environments where younger footballers could thrive. His Tottenham side became one of Europe’s best teams despite operating with fewer resources than many of their rivals, while his spell at Chelsea demonstrated an ability to stabilise a chaotic dressing room and extract improvement from a talented but unbalanced squad.

That experience feels particularly relevant at Manchester United. This is not a club requiring minor adjustments; it is a club still searching for a clear football identity. Pochettino has spent much of his career building exactly that.

Even the best coaches struggle when recruitment and management pull in different directions, and that, among other things is where Manchester United have repeatedly run into trouble.

Successive managers have inherited squads constructed for different styles of football. Players signed for one coach have remained when another arrived with entirely different ideas. The result has been an increasingly awkward collection of footballers who often appear unsuited to the system being asked of them.

If Pochettino is to succeed, that cycle cannot continue.

The club’s hierarchy must show the discipline to recruit according to a long-term strategy rather than chasing short-term fixes. That requires difficult decisions, particularly regarding players who may still carry reputations but no longer fit the demands of modern elite football.

Tottenham’s rise under Pochettino was possible because the squad gradually became an extension of the manager’s ideas. Manchester United have not reached that point under any coach since Sir Alex Ferguson.

Without alignment between the manager and recruitment department, even the strongest project stalls, and eventually fails.

Perhaps the greatest danger is expecting immediate transformation.

The temptation after years of disappointment will be to judge Pochettino’s reign through the lens of short-term results. That is understandable, especially when the club sits far below the standards many expect from them.

Yet rebuilding rarely follows a straight line. Pochettino’s first Tottenham team finished fifth before progressing into genuine title challengers, and Champions League finalists. Many of the players who later became stars required time and patience. The same principle is likely to apply at Old Trafford.

His opening fixture at Liverpool serves as a reminder of how much work remains to be done. Whatever happens at Anfield, it should not define the project. The more important question is whether United begin to look like a team with direction.

For all the doom that surrounds Manchester United, the club remains one of football’s great institutions. The fanbase remains enormous, the resources remain substantial, and the attraction of the badge has not disappeared yet.

Pochettino himself acknowledged that reality when discussing the scale of the support he encounters around the world. That is why the job continues to draw elite managerial candidates despite the obvious risks. The potential rewards remain extraordinary. The challenge is converting potential into reality.

The honest answer is yes, but only under conditions that have often been absent at Manchester United.

Pochettino has the coaching pedigree. He has the experience of handling demanding environments. He has a proven track record of improving players and building teams. Whether that is enough depends largely on whether the club has learned from the mistakes that consumed previous managers.

If United continue changing direction every couple of years, no coach will succeed. If they provide Pochettino with time, authority and recruitment aligned to a coherent football vision, then he may have a better chance than most of restoring the club to relevance at the top of the Premier League.

His first game – away to Liverpool – is obviously a daunting introduction to the task ahead. In many ways, it will be a good indicator of where Manchester United currently stand. They are beginning another chapter while measuring themselves against a rival that has spent years getting the fundamentals right.

Pochettino’s challenge is not simply to win matches. It is to ensure that, a few years from now, Manchester United are finally discussing how to compete for titles again rather than debating the future of yet another manager.

#1795. Liverpool handed unexpected boost ahead of Manchester United clash after lineup decision

Liverpool have received a surprise boost ahead of their Premier League showdown against Manchester United, with star striker Alexander Isak handed a rest while on international duty.

Sweden boss Graham Potter pledged to name a strong team against Poland for the Nations League B dead rubber - the Swedes already confirmed as group winners ahead of kick-off.

But despite that promise, Isak remained on the bench for the full 90 minutes on Tuesday night as Sweden secured a 1-1 draw in Poland to conclude a successful Nations League campaign.

Sweden will move up to the top tier of the Nations League for the 2028-29 edition of the competition, allowing Isak to mix with Europe’s elite on the international stage.

Isak missed three games for Sweden during the last international break after picking up a thigh issue, which then prevented the 27-year-old from featuring for Liverpool against Manchester City and LASK.

But rather than returning from international duty with an injury, this time Isak will come back to Merseyside fully rested for Sunday’s clash with Man United.

So far this season, Isak has made 14 appearances for Liverpool across all competitions, grabbing eight goals and one assist.

After an injury-frustrated debut season at Anfield - Isak suffering a fibula fracture in December - following his £130million move from Newcastle, the Swede has become a central figure to Andoni Iraola’s plans.

Aside from the two games he missed due to a thigh issue, Isak has played minutes in every fixture he has been available for.

Isak has only faced Man Utd once as a Liverpool player, taken off after 72 minutes at Anfield during a 2-1 defeat in October 2025 before missing the return fixture at Old Trafford due to an adductor issue.

Mauricio Pochettino has arrived at Carrington as he begins life as Manchester United manager, and he has ensured that training sessions are already underway.

The Manchester Evening News reports that Pochettino’s trusted lieutenants Jesus Perez, Toni Jimenez, and his son Sebastiano Pochettino carried out training at Carrington on Wednesday morning.

#1793. Mazzara: ‘A core of 16-18 high level players’ – Cardinale hopes to take Milan to new levels

Gerry Cardinale has invested heavily in AC Milan recently and there are no plans to slow down anytime soon.

Since the restructuring of the vendor loan, Cardinale has completely changed his ownership style. More actively involved, the American has seemingly fallen in love with the club and has become desperate to see it succeed.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Glimpses were seen before the mercato, with him regularly visiting the training ground. However, his work since then – spending €150 million on transfers and attending every Serie A game so far – shows the level of dedication he has to the cause.

In January, the American is expected to spend heavily, too. A €70 million bid for Endrick is being prepared, whilst he is also determined to sign Goncalo Inacio. It’s clear that he wants to raise the level of the starters and those who will contribute from the bench.

In an editorial for MilanNews today, Pietro Mazzara looked at the current squad and what Cardinale plans to do.

“AC Milan’s transfer market is poised for significant events because Gerry Cardinale has no intention of stopping. His comments in recent days, both public and private, are a clear statement of what the AC Milan owner intends to do to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“Whether he succeeds or not will only be determined by time and the type of decisions he makes, but he certainly has the desire, vision, and financial resources. One can expect anything from someone who beat out Netflix for the Warner Bros. acquisition.

“Among the many things he has learned is that the climate of mediocrity surrounding results has undermined the mentality of a club and an environment that, instead, must strive to always be at the top.

“But returning to those levels requires several factors: a clear decision-making structure (which will be finalised by Markus Krösche, who will always report to Cardinale, who will always have the final say and be involved in negotiations), strong players in the squad, a political presence in the halls of power, a connection with the fans, and credibility.

“What may seem like slogans in themselves are actually manifestos that one can legitimately believe or not. The only way to evaluate Cardinale’s work is to observe how he operates and then draw conclusions.

“He’s fired up, and between January and next summer there will be some serious transfer campaigns. The reason is simple: there’s a need to significantly raise the squad’s level, creating a core of 16-18 players of a certain caliber who can be joined by young players to develop and develop.

“This is why Milan will be looking for not only technically strong players, but also leaders who can complement those already in the Milan core group.

“It’s crucial to raise the team’s personality, including strong personalities who can provide a different kind of motivation during the day-to-day at Milanello. These players, inevitably, cost money, but Cardinale doesn’t want to set limits.

“This doesn’t mean Milan will sign a player worth one hundred million euros, but it does mean they can continue along the operational path laid out by Diego Moreira. All of this is in concert and in line with Ruben Amorim, who is fiercely defended by the AC Milan owner and with whom he intends to begin a long-term relationship.

“And the vision is to acquire the Van Dijks in the pre-prime phase rather than signing them at 35 (assuming, for the sake of argument, that I’d sign someone like that now).

“In my opinion, a Sandro Tonali- style signing is needed. And it’s not out of the question that Milan could try to bring him back in the coming years, even though he currently plays for a club as complex to negotiate with as Tottenham.

“Meanwhile, discussions are ongoing to finalise the renewal of Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse.”

#1792. Why Arsenal are the ideal destination for Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 10:28

Arsenal have been interested in the profile of Eli Junior Kroupi for many months, and the forward should be one of the talking points of the next January transfer window. The London club have everything to be the ideal destination for the young France international.

Author of a very good 2025-26 season with Bournemouth in his first year in the Premier League, Kroupi scored 13 goals in 33 league matches. The 20-year-old striker was a revelation and quickly appeared on the radar of Europe’s biggest clubs.

‘Last summer, a fifth metatarsal injury compromised a possible departure, which the player was considering,’ - RMC Sport reported. The French outlet says the former Lorient player will be one of the attractions of the next summer transfer window, as he still interests heavyweights.

Kroupi has only just returned from his injury, however. He has played just four cameos with Bournemouth, but he reminded everyone of the extent of his talent with France. The 20-year-old won his first two caps and scored his first goal for France against Turkey (2-1).

During that international gathering, the forward made an impression and is considered one of the positives. He is highly rated by Zinedine Zidane’s staff, RMC Sport points out. His status is therefore potentially already changing, and that is before his expected transfer next summer.

For this important next step in his career, Arsenal have everything to be the ideal destination. While PSG, Barcelona and Bayern Munich are also interested in his profile, Arsenal have been trying to sign him for many months. Mikel Arteta is described as a fan of the new France international by TalkSport.

A move to the London club would allow Kroupi to stay in the Premier League. It is the biggest league in the world and he has already found his feet there with his 13 goals in his first season. Arsenal also appear to be still looking for a number nine, with Kroupi seen as their ‘ideal candidate’.

Viktor Gyokeres has failed to establish himself at the London club.

A departure is already being talked about for the next January transfer window. Kroupi’s profile is also compatible with Arteta’s style of play, as the Frenchman is a quick, technical striker with a great eye for goal.

Joining Arsenal would allow Kroupi to take an important step in his career by joining a top club. The English side are back among Europe’s best teams after their Premier League title win and Champions League final last year. It is one of the most attractive projects, along with that of PSG, at the moment.

However, in Paris, competition is strong at the tip of the attack with 2025 Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembele, who is set to extend his contract. The problem is the same at Bayern Munich with their 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who has also signed a new deal.

In London, Kai Havertz, who can notably be repositioned behind the centre-forward, represents less and more accessible competition for Kroupi.

#1791. England’s potential path to glory proves Nations League is more difficult to win than the World Cup

Sometimes you have to say the unsayable because no one else will.

The Nations League is a more difficult competition to win than the World Cup or the European Championships. Stay with me.

Though there remain plenty of club football fans who take no interest in international football outside of major tournaments and are sceptical about the Nations League, there has been a noticeable drop in the number of club fans repeating the trite notion it is a pointless competition made up of glorified friendlies no one cares about.

My hunch as to why: people are beginning to realise how much of a refreshing addition to the football it really is, plus how many tasty fixtures it produces. And it is that final point — the competition regularly throwing up blockbuster clashes between European heavyweights — that explains why the Nations League might just be the hardest competition to win in international football.

A disclaimer is needed at this point. The Nations League is not a major tournament like the World Cup or European Championships are. Those competitions take place in single block international breaks during the summer (except when hosted in the Middle East) and the stakes at play mean immeasurably more pressure and psychological challenges as players and teams seek to win the trophies that matter most.

The World Cup and Euros remain more psychologically draining and patently more important. But more difficult to win than the Nations League in a footballing sense? Honestly, no.

The calibre of opposition is far higher in Europe’s newest event compared with the World Cup or Euros. Just look at Argentina’s route to the World Cup final where they were defeated by Spain.

They faced Algeria, Austria, debutants Jordan, fellow debutants Cape Verde, Egypt, Switzerland and then finally one world-football powerhouse, England, and were suddenly into a World Cup final.

For all their memories of their best World Cup finish since 1966, England’s route to their semi-final defeat to Argentina was not much more difficult. Croatia, Ghana, Panama, DR Congo, Mexico, and finally Norway.

And in their previous tournament, when England limped to the Euro 2024 final under Gareth Southgate with a string of uninspiring performances, they faced Serbia, Denmark, Slovenia, Slovakia, Switzerland and the Netherlands — and navigating that pretty presentable route meant they had qualified for the final and a shot at becoming European champions.

And what made this summer’s expanded World Cup even less likely to produce those big fixtures was FIFA’s brazenly cynical introduction of Wimbledon-styled protected ranking at its seeding stage.

The world’s four top-ranked nations would be kept apart in different quarters of the draw until the semi-finals providing they each won their groups. Shock: they all did.

Sure enough, for the first time in history the four top ranks made up the men’s World Cup semi-finalists: Argentina, England, France and Spain. A great product, just as FIFA wanted, but it had taken 100 matches to get there, the only blockbuster fixture among 72 group matches having been Spain and Uruguay, two former winners.

Winter energy bill misery on way as price cap set to jump by 26% in January

England’s Ivan Toney fails in bid to move assault trial over Euro 2028 clash

Nations League draw simulated as England get favourable quarter-final tie

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

The World Cup was great, but plenty of its matches had been rather too easy to call beforehand.

The calibre of opposition is far higher in Europe’s newest event compared with the World Cup or Euros

Now consider England’s potential path to Nations League glory next summer. A group stage first of all where England faced Czechia, Croatia and world champions Spain home and away.

Croatia are a good footballing nation but by finishing third of the group are now out, with next March to bring together only the winners and runners up from the four groups for the quarter-finals.

Group A3 winners England will face either Belgium, the Netherlands or Erling Haaland’s Norway — the teams ranked eighth, ninth and 19th in the world rankings.

After a two-legged tie against one of those opponents, England would gear up for next summer’s Nations League Finals, a one-off semi-final and then potentially a final, with France, Germany or Portugal as their likeliest opponents in those two games.

Here is a string of prestige fixtures far more testing for Thomas Tuchel’s side than the World Cup produced. No comparison in pressure and scrutiny, granted, but tougher in purely footballing terms, undoubtedly — and coaches are not rotating their teams or resting players as much as one might imagine. It is taken seriously.

For its sheer hit rate of big games out of the total set of fixtures and for how consistently well a top team would have to perform to navigate them all, the UEFA Nations League has become international football’s most difficult competition to win. There. Sometimes you have to say the unsayable because no one else will.

#1790. Why Manchester United kit selection vs Liverpool could be a good omen - with one glaring exception

Mauricio Pochettino has potentially been handed a positive omen for his first game in charge of Manchester United.

The Argentine begins his tenure as Red Devils boss with the daunting prospect of facing the club’s biggest rivals away from home, with the two sides in contrasting form.

Pochettino arrives at a club currently in the bottom three of the Premier League, while Andoni Iraola has Liverpool fourth in the Premier League table after 10 games.

For Sunday’s trip to Anfield, Man United have confirmed they will wear this season’s third kit which consists of white shirts and black shorts.

Interestingly, Man Utd’s four most recent victories at the home of their arch rivals have come with the players wearing white shirts, including the away half of last season’s double.

Harry Maguire’s header late on gave Man United a 2-1 win at Anfield, ending a run of 10 games without a win for Man United at Anfield.

To find further wins in white for Manchester United at Anfield you would have to go back to Louis van Gaal’s reign.

In 2016 Wayne Rooney’s strike sealed a smash-and-grab 1-0 win against Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool, with Juan Mata starring the year prior.

However, fans will recall that Man United wore white when they were embarrassed 7-0 at Anfield in March 2023.

Coincidentally, Man Utd are undefeated at Anfield since that humbling loss, picking up two draws and a win in their last three visits to Liverpool. On those occasions Man Utd wore all white.

There was a large gap between white strips for Manchester United on trips to Anfield, with a six-year wait between a 2-0 defeat in the Europa League in 2016 and a 4-0 hammering in 2022.

#1789. Mauricio Pochettino urges Pep Guardiola to take USA job after revealing talks that sparked Man United U-turn

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 11:04

Outgoing USA manager Mauricio Pochettino has publicly advised Pep Guardiola to pursue the vacant national team job as he prepares to begin his new role at Manchester United.

The 54-year-old Argentine will bid an emotional farewell to the Stars and Stripes when he takes charge of his final fixture against Haiti on Tuesday before officially taking over from Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

With the US Soccer Federation now searching for a successor, former Manchester City boss Guardiola has emerged as a ‘top target’ for the vacant managerial role.

Addressing the media during his final pre-match press conference, Pochettino gave his endorsement to the legendary Catalan coach - who won 20 trophies across 10 seasons at Man City - and urged him to accept an offer if approached.

"Take it," Pochettino told reporters. "Why? Because it’s a perfect moment to arrive at the federation.

“Everything is on the right path, in the right direction. Of course, take it. Of course, you are going to find really good players, good people – the players can fit his style."

While Pochettino is backing Guardiola for international management, a previous conversation between the pair helped trigger the Argentine's own return to the club game.

Last week, Man United confirmed Pochettino as their new head coach after dismissing Carrick, who has left the Red Devils languishing in the Premier League relegation zone following a dismal start to the campaign.

Taking the reins at Carrington marks Pochettino's first club appointment since departing Chelsea at the conclusion of the 2023-24 season, adding to previous English top-flight stints with Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur.

Pochettino was given the green light by Man United to see out his USA commitments first, with his final outing against Haiti largely a formality after the Stars and Stripes secured a dominant 6-0 win in the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday.

In an interview with The Telegraph ahead of his departure, Pochettino disclosed that he confessed to Guardiola how much he longed for the daily routine of club football when the pair met at an MLS game between New York Red Bulls and New York City FC in September.

“I am ready [to return],” Pochettino explained. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything… this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

Pochettino’s candid remarks about craving a Premier League comeback may frustrate some USA supporters, given that he had put pen to paper on a new four-year contract extension just one month before his discussion with Guardiola.
